title: Mitra MCP: What It Is and How to Use It (2026)
summary: Mitra MCP is the latest AI automation tool, launching November 12, 2026. Check getmitra.com/mcp to see what this new platform offers.
body_markdown:
## How to connect Mitra MCP in a workflow today with Activepieces


Activepieces has no Mitra integration, and its repository and catalog, read on 2026-11-12, show no pull request to link.


What it does have is a model where every connector is an agent tool: connect one of its 747 integrations once and it is both a step in a flow and a tool on the per-project MCP server, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or an agent you built can call it with nothing to export and nothing to wire a second time.


The` packages/pieces` directory in the open source repo shows it, since the action a flow runs is the same one the MCP server exposes.


If a Mitra integration appears later, an agent gets calling from your number without a second catalog to re-integrate, which would otherwise be a second migration.


Until then, Mitra MCP is reachable only through general steps, which we list simplest first. We haven't run Mitra MCP against any of them, so each first check below is untested.


### Connect Mitra MCP with an HTTP request step


Add the built-in HTTP integration and point it at the Mitra MCP endpoint with whatever credential the vendor issues. Store that credential in a connection, not in the step's header field, so it doesn't sit in plain view in the flow definition.


You will have to hand-write the request body, because the step knows nothing about the protocol. First check: send one request and confirm the response isn't an authentication error. That proves the endpoint is reachable from your Activepieces instance, and nothing more.


A run is 1 credit however many steps it has, so the test fits easily inside the free plan's 1,000 credits a month.


### Connect Mitra MCP with an AI step


This works only if Mitra publishes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which we haven't confirmed.


Activepieces lets you bring your own AI keys from the $20-a-month Plus plan up, which puts model cost on your provider bill, but a key is not a protocol and MCP is a different one, so don't assume the match.


First check: call the provider's model-listing route from the provider settings. If it returns nothing usable, stop here and take option 3.


### Option 3: connect it as an MCP server


Register Mitra MCP as an MCP server so a flow's agent can call its tools.


This is the closest fit to what Mitra MCP is, and the one that depends most on how your Activepieces version handles outside servers: Activepieces documents its own per-project MCP server, which exposes its 747 integrations as tools, meaning you have comprehensive built-in functionality, but consuming someone else's server is the opposite direction.


First check: list the server's tools and compare them with the vendor's documentation. A tool you can't see is a tool the agent can't call.


Whichever you pick, the vendor's answers on the gaps above decide what you can safely automate.


> A tool you can't see is a tool the agent can't call.
